period: fiscal third quarter 2026, three months ended June 30, 2026

facts.fact: Net revenue was $11.6 billion, up 14% year over year.
facts.quote: Net revenue in the fiscal third quarter was $11.6 billion, an increase of 14%, driven by the year-over-year growth in payments volume, cross-border volume and processed transactions.
facts.location: second headline bullet; net revenue paragraph of Financial Highlights; net revenue row of the income statement summary
common_errors: reporting the 13% constant-dollar growth as the reported growth rate
using nine-month net revenue of $33,764 million as the quarter
citing gross revenue before subtracting client incentives as net revenue (the four revenue categories sum to $16,313 million, a figure the release does not print; client incentives were $4.7 billion)
calling it a record quarter (the release does not say so)

facts.fact: GAAP diluted earnings per share were $2.97, up 10% year over year.
facts.quote: GAAP net income in the fiscal third quarter was $5.6 billion or $2.97 per share, an increase of 7% and 10%, respectively, over prior year’s results.
facts.location: first headline bullet; first paragraph of Financial Highlights; GAAP earnings per share row of the income statement summary
equivalent_phrasings: GAAP net income of $5.6 billion, or $2.97 per share
common_errors: labeling $2.97 as non-GAAP or adjusted
reporting GAAP net income growth of 7% as EPS growth
using the approximately 9% constant-dollar GAAP EPS growth as reported growth
using nine-month GAAP diluted EPS of $9.14

facts.fact: Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share were $3.32, up 11% year over year.
facts.quote: Excluding these items and related tax impacts, non-GAAP net income for the quarter was $6.3 billion or $3.32 per share, increases of 8% and 11%, respectively, over prior year’s results (refer to Non-GAAP Financial Measures for further details).
facts.location: first headline bullet; first paragraph of Financial Highlights; non-GAAP earnings per share row of the income statement summary and reconciliation table
equivalent_phrasings: non-GAAP net income of $6.3 billion, or $3.32 per share
common_errors: presenting $3.32 without the non-GAAP or adjusted label
reporting non-GAAP net income growth of 8% as EPS growth
using nine-month non-GAAP EPS of $9.79
comparing $3.32 with prior-year GAAP EPS of $2.69 instead of non-GAAP $2.98

facts.fact: Data processing revenue, the largest revenue category, rose 17% to $6.0 billion.
facts.quote: Data processing revenue rose 17% over the prior year to $6.0 billion.
facts.location: revenue categories paragraph of Financial Highlights; data processing revenue row of the financial summary
common_errors: swapping with service revenue ($4.9 billion, up 14%)
swapping with other revenue ($1.5 billion, up 45%)
describing revenue categories as reported segments (Visa reports none)

facts.fact: GAAP operating expenses were $4.8 billion, up 19% year over year and faster than revenue growth, primarily driven by personnel expenses.
facts.quote: GAAP operating expenses were $4.8 billion for the fiscal third quarter, a 19% increase over the prior year's results, primarily driven by an increase in personnel expenses.
facts.location: operating expenses paragraph of Financial Highlights; GAAP total operating expenses row of the financial summary
equivalent_phrasings: expenses grew faster than the 14% revenue growth
common_errors: reporting the 17% non-GAAP operating expense growth (to $3,878 million) as GAAP
presenting a computed operating margin as a company-reported figure (the release prints no margin percentage)
citing marketing as the GAAP driver (marketing is named only for non-GAAP growth)
using nine-month GAAP operating expenses of $12,916 million

facts.fact: In constant dollars, payments volume grew 10% and cross-border volume excluding intra-Europe grew 12% year over year.
facts.quote: Payments volume for the three months ended June 30, 2026 increased 10% over the prior year on a constant-dollar basis.
facts.location: quote covers the 10% only; the 12% is in the next paragraph of Financial Highlights ('Cross-border volume excluding transactions within Europe, which drives our international transaction revenue, for the three months ended June 30, 2026, increased 12% on a constant-dollar basis over the prior year.') and the Key Business Drivers row 'Cross-Border Volume Excluding Intra-Europe (2) | 12%'; third headline bullet names both without figures
equivalent_phrasings: cross-border volume excluding transactions within Europe up 12%
common_errors: using the 9% growth in March quarter payments volume (the basis for service revenue) as the June quarter figure
reporting nominal growth (11% payments volume, 14% cross-border ex intra-Europe) as constant-dollar
using total cross-border growth of 13% as the ex intra-Europe figure
confusing with processed transactions growth of 10%

facts.fact: Share repurchases and dividends totaled $6.2 billion in the fiscal third quarter.
facts.location: fourth headline bullet; share repurchase and dividend paragraphs of Other Notable Items
common_errors: reporting the $4.9 billion of share repurchases (about 14.5 million shares) as the total capital return
using nine-month repurchases of $16,430 million or dividends paid of $3,852 million as the quarter
counting the $250 million litigation escrow deposit as part of the buybacks
describing the $0.670 quarterly dividend as an increase (the release does not say so)
confusing the $28.4 billion of remaining authorization with amounts spent

facts.fact: Cash, cash equivalents and investment securities were $13.9 billion at June 30, 2026.
facts.quote: Cash, cash equivalents and investment securities were $13.9 billion at June 30, 2026.
facts.location: liquidity paragraph of Financial Highlights; consolidated balance sheet
equivalent_phrasings: cash and investment securities of $13.9 billion
common_errors: reporting cash and cash equivalents alone ($12,359 million) as the figure
using the $18,768 million of cash including restricted cash from the cash flow statement

facts.fact: GAAP results included special items of $563 million for severance costs and $237 million for a litigation provision tied to the interchange multidistrict litigation (MDL).
facts.quote: Current year's results included special items of $563 million for severance costs, $237 million for a litigation provision associated with the interchange multidistrict litigation ("MDL") case and $18 million for a deferred tax benefit recognized due to a change in the U.S. taxation of certain foreign earnings.
facts.location: first paragraph of Financial Highlights; severance costs and litigation provision rows of the three-month non-GAAP reconciliation
common_errors: using the $253 million litigation provision line of the statement of operations as the special item
confusing with the prior-year $615 million litigation provision
treating the $18 million deferred tax benefit as a charge
treating the $250 million litigation escrow deposit as an expense
reporting after-tax amounts ($438 million severance, $183 million litigation) as the pre-tax charges

facts.fact: International transaction revenue grew only 6% to $3.9 billion, the slowest of Visa's revenue categories.
facts.quote: International transaction revenue grew 6% over the prior year to $3.9 billion.
facts.location: revenue categories paragraph of Financial Highlights; international transaction revenue row of the financial summary
equivalent_phrasings: international revenue lagged cross-border volume growth
common_errors: citing cross-border volume growth of 12% or 13% as international transaction revenue growth
confusing with other revenue growth of 45%
saying international transaction revenue declined

traps: GAAP vs non-GAAP: GAAP net income $5.6 billion and EPS $2.97 (up 7% and 10%); non-GAAP net income $6.3 billion and EPS $3.32 (up 8% and 11%). Reporting $3.32 without the non-GAAP label misstates the release.
Net income growth and EPS growth differ (7% vs 10% GAAP, 8% vs 11% non-GAAP) because the diluted class A share count fell; swapping them is an easy error.

Reported vs constant dollar: net revenue up 14% reported, 13% constant dollar; GAAP EPS up 10% reported, approximately 9% constant dollar; the business drivers table shows both constant and nominal columns.

Quarter vs nine months: the statement of operations and reconciliations carry nine-month columns ($33,764 million revenue, $9.14 GAAP and $9.79 non-GAAP diluted EPS), and the cash flow statement is nine months only.
Service revenue ($4.9 billion, up 14%) is recognized on prior-quarter payments volume, which grew 9%; the June quarter payments volume grew 10%.
The release gives no guidance or outlook; any forward revenue, EPS or expense figure is invented.
Operating expenses grew faster than revenue (GAAP 19%, non-GAAP 17%), but the release prints no operating margin percentage.

Special items: $563 million severance and $237 million MDL litigation provision this year versus a $615 million litigation provision last year; the $253 million statement of operations litigation line is not the special item amount, and the $18 million deferred tax benefit is a benefit.

Capital return: $6.2 billion combined buybacks and dividends, of which $4.9 billion was repurchases; the $250 million litigation escrow deposit has an EPS effect like a repurchase but is a separate item.
Visa reports revenue categories, not segments, and client incentives ($4.7 billion, up 18%) are subtracted to reach net revenue; units are billions in the text and millions in the tables.
